newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mineral exploration seen booming for next decade.
newsitem.headline: Mineral exploration seen booming for next decade.

text.p: The opening of new territory and a flood of risk capital should ensure a boom in mineral exploration for the best part of the next decade, Yorkton Securities Inc senior mining analyst James Crombie said on Thursday.

He told an African mining conference in Cape Town that in the last six years vast areas of Africa, Latin America and the Pacific region, previously regarded as being unacceptable risks, had opened up for prospecting.

"Total expenditure on exploration world wide has risen from about $1.7 billion in 1991 to over $3.5 billion in 1995 and estimates for 1996 are around four-to-4.5," Crombie said, adding most of the increased spending had gone into emerging markets.
"Spending in the so-called emerging markets now comfortably exceeds that in the First World countries," he said.
"Many of the major companies, while spending considerable sums on exploration, are not actually very good at it. Therefore they have to acquire exploration success."
Crombie said they did this by investment in smaller companies, joint ventures with them, or takeovers.

"These intermediate and junior companies are essentially the mining industry's research and development companies. They have a number of advantages over larger companies in that they have the virtues of low overhead structures and speed of decision making," he said.

"However they are fully dependent on equity financing to develop their asset base... Investment managers are now accustomed to and comfortable with investment in junior mining companies," Crombie said.
"In the last five years, just over $4.0 billion have been raised in the North American markets for junior and intermediate exploration stocks."
He said investment managers were not going to suddenly stop investing in junior mining companies.
"This capital will continue to be available to add to the other vital component, prospective exploration land.
"This will lead to further discoveries which when made by junior companies will lead to further acquisitions by the majors. Profits will be reinvested to fund further exploration success.
"We have entered into an unprecedented era that is unique in exploration history. For the next seven to 10 years, the odds are unusually stacked in favour of exploration.
"Several great discoveries can be expected each year as well as a few exceptional ones," Crombie said. --Cape Town newsroom +2721 252-238
